items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...there were some Louis Armstrong cuts on the other side because he was in the movie.

ctx.x: quartet was with Hamp. So I started playing that music. So I mean it was all subsumed. It was subsumed as just being jazz.

That’s so interesting, because I had the same experience with the soundtrack from the Glenn Miller movie. A big band, and there were some Louis Armstrong cuts on the other side because he was in the movie.

It’s funny you would say that because Moe Purtill, the original drummer with the Glenn Miller band, who is on that, sat right here and played drums. He came with a friend of mine and my father played piano over there, I played the bass, and Moe was right there. What a thrill. I mean I met Moe and we became good friends. He was one of my heroes too because one Christmas I got that little deluxe edition 45s of the Glenn Miller edition with Moe Purtill and that was one of the records that I had when I got that set…
